title: The Tech Desk with Ronnie
description: Ronnie reads your real gadget woes aloud and fixes every single one by yelling at the device. Barry owns a working router and is steamrolled for it.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on Snazzie FM, and welcome back to the Tech Desk, where your gadgets are broken and I am, frankly, the only man brave enough to talk back to them. No callers tonight, folks. You wrote in, I read it, I solve it. That's the system.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, I do want to say, gently, before we start, that I... I actually own a router that works.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And that's wonderful for you, Barry, but the people need help, not bragging. Let's get into the mailbag.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: First one. Maria from the laundromat writes, quote, I dropped my phone and now there's a thin line across the screen, right over my kids' photos, and I'm terrified of losing them, end quote. Oh, Maria.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: A line on the line. Classic. That's a phone-line issue, sweetheart, that's your landline acting up. Here's what you do. You pick up that phone, and you firmly tell it that you are not afraid of it.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, it's a touchscreen. There's no landline. The screen is cracked.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Which is exactly why it needs to hear your voice, Barry. A touchscreen responds to touch and tone. <p:0.3> Maria, give it a stern talking-to. A nice firm voice. Let it know who's holding it.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That will not fix a crack.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Next letter. Dev, who works nights, writes, quote, my Wi-Fi drops every evening around nine, I can't finish my online classes, and I already paid for the whole semester, end quote.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Drops at nine, you say. <p:0.3> Dev, your router is tired. It's stayed up too late, it's cranky, and it's clocking out. Put it to bed at eight. Tuck it in. An earlier bedtime, that's your fix.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Routers do not get tired, Ronnie. That's evening congestion, everyone in the building is online at nine, it's a channel problem...

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Or, and hear me out, you give it a good firm holler so it doesn't get comfortable. A tired router that's also a little scared? That router works the night shift, Dev. <p:0.3> And speaking of working hard, tonight's segment is brought to you by Big Mike's Subs, where the meatball never quits on you.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: You just plugged a sandwich into a Wi-Fi question.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Folks come to me for results. Barry, read the next one, my throat's getting warmed up for the hollering portion.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Alright. Glenda, retired, writes, quote, my late husband's old laptop has the only copy of our wedding video and it won't turn on anymore. I just want to see him again, end quote. <p:0.3> Ronnie, this one's serious. She should take that to a proper data recovery shop.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Nonsense, Barry, that's expensive. Glenda, sweetheart, here's the warm and loving fix, free of charge. You take that laptop outside, you lay it gently in the sun, and you let it warm its memories back up. Memories are stored in warmth, Glenda. Everyone knows that.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Please do not put it in the sun, Glenda. That is the opposite of...

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And once it's good and warm, you lean in nice and close, and you call his name to it, real loving, the way you used to. Help it remember the man. A laptop, Glenda, is just a battery that misses people.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, that is... a laptop does not miss people. Glenda, I am begging you, take it to a proper shop, they can pull the file off the drive.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And if a loving call won't do it, Barry, she gives it one good firm holler, and that laptop boots right up out of respect. Moving on. Trent, small business owner.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Trent writes, quote, ransomware locked all my invoices, the message demands payment in crypto by Friday or I lose everything, end quote. Oh, Trent. I've been there.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: You have never been there.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: This is exactly like when my microwave held my burrito hostage. Wouldn't open the door, beeping at me, demands. So I unplugged it overnight. By morning? It forgot it ever had leverage. Unplug the hackers, Trent.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: You cannot unplug hackers. They're not in the wall, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And don't pay them money. Pay them a five-star review. Be the bigger man. Leave them five stars, write, great service, very firm, and they'll feel terrible and give your invoices back.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: [surprise-ah] Ronnie. That is a federal... that is a crime in progress, you're telling a man to negotiate with...

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And if the review doesn't land, Trent, you scream at the screen. Loud. So they hear it through the internet. Last letter of the night, Barry, and it's a doozy.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Patricia from the marina writes, quote, my brand-new smart fridge keeps ordering forty cartons of oat milk it thinks I want, and now my porch is a wall of oat milk, end quote.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Patricia, that fridge has gone feral. There's no talking to it now. It's tasted freedom. <p:0.3> So here's the only humane option left.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Oh no.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You take it out to the yard. You dig a respectful hole. And you scream at it, OUTDOORS, where the whole street can see, so every neighbor witnesses exactly who is in charge. I call this rebooting it spiritually.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: You're telling a woman to bury a refrigerator.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: In the YARD, Barry. <p:0.3> Not in the house. I'm not a monster.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That distinction does not help her.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: We've got time for one quick follow-up. Barry, you read it, I'm savoring this water.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Fine. Dennis writes, quote, took your advice last week, screamed at my modem. The modem's fine. But the police came, end quote. <p:0.3> He says the modem witnessed everything. Ronnie, the modem is now a witness.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And that, Barry, <p:0.3> is the most coherent connection that man has had all year. We'll be right back.
